paper: Civic Paper No. 01: The Leeds Water Guarantee

claims.claim: The Government's water bill was announced in the King's Speech (13 May 2026) as the Clean Water Bill; on 29 September 2026 the Prime Minister said the strengthened Water Bill will remove the 1–3% caps on government shareholdings set under the Water Act 1989, and that mayors will gain powers.
claims.check: Has the bill been introduced? Its formal name, current stage on bills.parliament.uk, whether the share-cap removal and mayoral powers are in it, and Royal Assent.

claims.claim: A 10-year plan for Britain, setting out stronger public control of water, is due 'later this year' (said 29 September 2026).
claims.check: Has it been published? If so, what does it say about water affordability, social tariffs or local control?

claims.claim: In January 2026 the Government decided against a national social tariff.
claims.check: Has a national or compulsory social tariff since been announced, legislated or amended into a bill?

claims.claim: The White Paper commits to replacing Ofwat with a single regulator.
claims.check: Has the new regulator been named or established? Update references to 'the regulator' or Ofwat where needed.

claims.claim: On 23 October 2026 the Environment Secretary said the Government will intervene in the next price review.
claims.check: Has the Government published its direction or strategic policy statement for the next price review? Does it include affordability or essential-volume objectives? Confirm the post-holder is still Environment Secretary.

claims.claim: Eight regional water councils announced 5 November 2026; local leaders' proposals on how they run are due by the end of 2026.
claims.check: Membership and remit of the Yorkshire council; whether the deadline has moved; whether West Yorkshire has submitted. After 31 December 2026 Decision 1 is out of date and needs rewording.

claims.claim: Kelda Holdings is owned 42% EQT, 42% GIC, 16% TCorp; EQT's purchase was reported to value Kelda at about £9.4bn, roughly 90% of RCV.
claims.check: Any change of shareholding, government stake, special administration or major refinancing.

claims.claim: The paper addresses the Mayor of West Yorkshire, the Secretary of State for Environment and HM Government by office, not by name.
claims.check: Confirm the offices still exist under those titles (e.g. a department renamed or a mayoralty changed).

claims.claim: Yorkshire Water 2026/27 metered tariffs: water £2.1838/m³, sewerage £2.9761/m³ on 95% of supply, standing charges £54.10 and £33.85.
claims.check: Have 2027/28 charges been published (usually February–March)? A new tariff year changes the model's base year and most figures.

claims.claim: Average Yorkshire Water household bill £636 in 2026/27.
6.8% of households in England and Wales in water poverty (over 5%), 15% over 3%, median gap £337 (2024/25).
claims.check: Has the Consumer Council for Water (or its successor) published newer figures, or any Leeds or Yorkshire estimate?

claims.claim: About 2.3 million households on water social tariffs (November 2026); Yorkshire Water contributes £2.5m in 2026/27.
claims.check: Newer counts or company contribution figures.

claims.claim: Average household use in England 136.9 litres per person per day (2025/26).
claims.check: Has the Environment Agency published a newer annual figure?
